summary: Hold: the table presents model-specific settings as environment-wide controls and gives the table-inclusion path for views and relationships, which use different controls. Microsoft also documents an environment switch covering semantic modeling, contradicting the reported gap.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-10-20T23:00:34.
The semantic model gives agents and Copilot a shared business-aware understanding of Dataverse data.
claims.quote: The Dataverse semantic model gives AI agents and Copilot experiences a shared, business-aware understanding of your Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable or disable semantic model generation across an environment.
claims.quote: Environment level | Enable or disable a semantic model generation across the entire environment via Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Individual signal types can be enabled or disabled.
claims.quote: Signal-type level | Enable or disable specific signal types across all tables (for example, disable sample data rows globally).

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Sensitive or regulated tables can be excluded from a semantic model.
claims.quote: When a table contains sensitive, regulated, or irrelevant data, you can exclude it from the semantic model without disabling the entire signal type.

claims.claim: The semantic model is on automatically in the enabled environments described by the briefing.
claims.quote: The platform automatically provisions the semantic model when you enable Copilot experiences over Dataverse data, so you don't need to set up anything manually to start.
claims.fix: Keep the conditional automatic-provisioning explanation. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/default-settings for automatic Work IQ enablement and its EU/EFTA, government-related and nonproduction exceptions; also acknowledge that settings-features still lists Dataverse intelligence switches as Off rather than silently harmonising the sources.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate licence or charge for semantic-model generation is not published in the feature documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model licensing pricing; opened semantic-model-overview, fine-tune-semantic-model-signals, semantic-model-faq, Work IQ understand-costs and api-overview. No separate generation licence or rate stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consuming Copilot Studio agents have their own licensing and Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage. You calculate the total cost based on the sum of the Copilot Credits your organization uses.
claims.fix: Cite this billing page rather than relying only on the semantic-model pages. Say consuming experiences may incur their own charges; keep that separate from the unpublished charge for model generation, and qualify that billing depends on the consuming experience and entitlement.

claims.claim: More > Semantic model > Configuration > Include in semantic model controls tables, views and relationships.
claims.quote: Select Views or select Relationships to see the table's associated views and relationships. Find the item you want to exclude and turn it On or Off.
claims.fix: Limit this row to table inclusion: More > Semantic model > model > Configuration > table > Include in semantic model, followed by Save and sync. Add a separate item-control path: More > Semantic model > model > Configuration > table > Views or Relationships > item > On or Off. Mention Discover all if Semantic model is missing from More.

claims.claim: The maker table, view and relationship settings apply across the environment.
claims.quote: Changes you make to a semantic model, including signal settings, table-level controls, and glossary entries, only apply to that specific semantic model. They don't affect other semantic models in your environment.
claims.fix: Change the row's scope to other and explain that it governs the selected semantic model, not every model in the environment. Tell administrators to review each relevant model and its associated apps or agents.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for changing the existing model's signal, table-inclusion or item toggles.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "semantic model" "signals" "API"; opened fine-tune-semantic-model-signals and ask/manage-semantic-models. Ask documents list/create/delete, but directs signal and existing-table tuning to Power Apps.

claims.claim: The System Administrator security role can manage the semantic model.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Semantic Model and Environment Maker

claims.claim: The Semantic Model and Environment Maker roles together can manage the semantic model.
claims.quote: You need either of the following security roles to manage the semantic model: System Administrator -or- Semantic Model and Environment Maker

claims.claim: Work IQ is configured in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: In the Manage pane, select Environments. On the Environments page, select an environment. In the command bar, select Settings. Expand Product, and then select Features.
claims.fix: Retain the path and add settings-features as a source for its Environments step. The cited manage-participation page documents the remainder, including Work IQ, but abbreviates navigation to 'Select Manage, and select the environment'.

claims.claim: The Work IQ environment feature switch governs the availability of semantic models in that environment.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ features in the environments where you want to use semantic models, search indexing, business skills, and the Business Applications paths in the Work IQ MCP.
claims.fix: Rename this row to 'Work IQ features, including semantic modeling, in the environment'. Explain that enabling features is distinct from environment data participation, and that participation settings do not prevent agentic access to underlying data.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell equivalent for the Work IQ environment feature switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "environment" "PowerShell" "setting" and "Work IQ" "environment" "API" "disable" settings; opened manage-participation and default-settings. Results describe UI configuration, not an equivalent environment-switch API.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and api; controls[2].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft provides no documented navigation path or automation for disabling semantic modeling at environment level.
claims.quote: The Work IQ setting turns on business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. If you turn off this setting, these features aren't available in the environment.
claims.fix: Merge this row with the Work IQ feature-switch row: Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ > Off. Explain that this is a broader switch, not a separately documented generation-only toggle. Keep automation null only for that narrowly defined equivalent.

claims.claim: Table relationships contribute semantic signals.
claims.quote: Table relationships | How records across tables are associated, such as one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.

claims.claim: Public views and sub-grid views contribute semantic signals.
claims.quote: Views | Public views with join conditions and sub-grid views that define which records and columns are relevant for a scenario.

claims.claim: The model extracts form names.
claims.quote: For forms, only the display name is captured.

claims.claim: Descriptions of tables and columns contribute semantic understanding.
claims.quote: Description summaries | Descriptions added to tables and columns that explain what they represent.

claims.claim: Sample data rows are an optional source of signals.
claims.quote: The semantic model automatically extracts signals from metadata that already exists in your Dataverse environment - table relationships, views, forms, column description summaries, and optionally sample data rows.

claims.claim: Makers can inspect generated understanding per table in Power Apps and identify gaps.
claims.quote: View generated semantic knowledge per entity — including name, description, and sample questions — directly in the Power Apps maker portal. Search for understanding gaps

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Makers can add glossary entries for domain-specific terms and acronyms.
claims.quote: The glossary allows makers to add domain-specific terms, acronyms, synonyms, and definitions that system signals can't infer.

claims.claim: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours.
claims.quote: The semantic model regenerates automatically every 12 hours to reflect schema changes.

claims.claim: Manual regeneration is available.
claims.quote: You can also trigger a manual regeneration at any time.

claims.claim: Initial generation can take up to two hours.
claims.quote: Initial generation can take up to two hours, and incremental changes typically take up to 30 minutes.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Automatic extraction reduces manual setup for agents.
claims.quote: Reduced setup time — The model automatically extracts semantic knowledge from your existing Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: Agents sharing a semantic model share its understanding and give more consistent answers.
claims.quote: When multiple agents reference the same semantic model, they share the same understanding of your data and return consistent responses across experiences.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Provisioning happens automatically when the relevant Dataverse intelligence or Copilot experience is enabled.
claims.quote: Once Dataverse intelligence is enabled, the semantic model is provisioned automatically.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Sample data rows are disabled by default.
claims.quote: The sample data rows signal is disabled by default.

claims.claim: Enabling sample rows makes example data available for semantic extraction.
claims.quote: When enabled, the system uses sample data to read and extract the metadata contained in the sample data rows.

claims.claim: The feature documentation does not describe a separate security-enforcement mechanism for the semantic model.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse semantic model security roles row column security; read overview, tuning, FAQ, Work IQ overview and Ask model management. Existing Dataverse permissions are described, not a separate semantic-model enforcement mechanism.

claims.claim: The semantic model does not itself take actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse semantic model" "actions"; opened semantic-model-overview, fine-tune-semantic-model-signals and business-applications-work-iq. They describe grounding and reasoning but do not expressly state this negative.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical negative with the documented scope: 'The semantic model supplies business context for agent reasoning; review action capabilities and approvals in each consuming agent.'

claims.claim: Computed signals are read-only.
claims.quote: Computed signals are read-only. You can't directly edit an artifact generated by the system.

claims.claim: Glossary definitions can correct system-generated understanding.
claims.quote: To override system-generated understanding, use the Glossary to add a corrected definition.

claims.claim: Changes apply to all agents or experiences sharing the selected model.
claims.quote: If multiple apps or agents share the same semantic model (for example, Sales Agent and Copilot in Dynamics 365 Sales both use SalesSpecificQnA), changes to that model apply to all experiences associated with it.

claims.claim: Underlying consumption-based services may continue to incur fees during preview.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP is a named semantic-model consumer.
claims.quote: a semantic model that powers agent experiences across Microsoft, including Dataverse MCP, Copilot in Power Apps, Microsoft Copilot, Sales Agent, and any agent built with Microsoft Copilot Studio over Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Copilot in Power Apps consumes semantic models over Dataverse data.
claims.quote: Copilot in Power Apps — Available in model-driven apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse consumes the semantic model.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot with Dataverse — Connects Microsoft Copilot to your Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 is a semantic-model consumer.
claims.quote: Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 — Uses Dataverse data to power sales scenarios.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents using Dataverse tables as knowledge sources consume semantic models.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio agents over Dataverse data — Agents built in Copilot Studio that use Dataverse tables as a knowledge source.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented regeneration, tuning and default behaviour describes the preview implementation.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] This is a preview feature.
claims.fix: Add 'The following behaviour and controls are documented for the preview and remain subject to change' before describing them. Distinguish the roadmap's In development status and target dates from Learn's available preview documentation.

claims.claim: The review action rating fits a capability that changes nothing until an administrator or maker chooses it.
claims.quote: action: "review"; defaultState: "on"; "the model is provisioned automatically when Copilot experiences over Dataverse are enabled"; targetDate: "November CY2026"
claims.fix: Set action to act-now for affected enabled environments: the page rates risk medium and describes automatic provisioning with a target in the run month. Cite default-settings, which also documents automatic enablement for eligible existing environments starting November 2026, and preserve its exceptions.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review has a corresponding control row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Keep sample data rows off" and "Review glossary entries and disabled signals quarterly". Rows cover table inclusion, Work IQ participation and an environment generation switch only.
claims.fix: Add rows for signal-type/sample-row settings and glossary management. The tuning page gives model > How your data is understood > Sample table rows > On or Off > Save, and model > Glossary; cite fine-tune-semantic-model-signals. Keep model-specific scope explicit.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Costs can vary through the consuming agents or services rather than a published dedicated semantic-generation meter.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.
claims.fix: Cite understand-costs and make the cost rationale start 'Variable.' Explain that Copilot Credit consumption belongs to the consuming experience, while separate semantic-generation pricing is not published. Do not describe the whole billing treatment as unpublished: licensed Copilot Chat grounding and Work IQ API consumption already have documented treatments.
